text: This report responds to direction from the Board of Health to review the feasibility of adding an Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) indicator to the Population Health Status Indicators (PHSI) dashboard. Intimate Partner Violence is a significant societal issue that has direct and ongoing impacts on victims, survivors, and families, and on overall community safety in Toronto. Intimate Partner Violence data that is accessible and publicly shared to understand its impacts can inform prevention efforts and support evidence-based decision making. Toronto Public Health (TPH) reports on a series of Population Health Status Indicators to support its mission to reduce health inequities, improve population health and to meet the requirements of the Ontario Public Health Standards. The Board of Health: 1. Requested the Ontario Ministry of Health and Ontario Health to establish and implement a province-wide, trauma-informed standard for improving the accuracy and consistency of collecting Intimate Partner Violence data in hospital settings within the existing mandatory emergency department reporting system (NACRS). 2. Requested Statistics Canada conduct ongoing population prevalence surveys of intimate partner violence to support local public health agencies to assess local trends and the impact of interventions.
